subject: QBR play: runway rollup, consolidated forecast, and account walk-throughs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR play: runway rollup, consolidated forecast, and account walk-throughs

Team —

We have the QBR presentation next Wednesday. I pulled an initial master workbook (attached) that rolls account-level runways into our consolidated forecast. I need two things from each of you by EOD Wednesday:

1) Account one-pagers (tight) for your top 6 accounts: current ARR, next 90-day asks, procurement blockers, principal admin contact, and required exec attendees for a potential close. Zip them into acct-onepagers.zip and drop into the Drive folder in the link below.

2) A confidence tier for each commitment in the forecast: High / Medium / Low, and a one-line rationale. We will show the confidence buckets on slide 6.

Notes on the workbook: the "runway" tab includes a roll-forward of committed revenue vs. at-risk amounts; the "ops" tab flags infra or SSO items that block launches. I left a few placeholder comments for Acme Corp and GammaHealth — please update directly.

Attachments: QBR_runway_master_v3.xlsx (master workbook, tabs: runway, ops, deal_lines)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR_Master_Runway
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/HS-8921-Acme

Connor
Connor O'Brien
VP, Sales Strategy & Ops | Redwood Inference
p: 415-555-0182

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR play: runway rollup, consolidated forecast, and account walk-throughs

Connor / all —

Uploading acct-onepagers.zip now (contains PDF one-pagers for Acme, Nebula, Orion Health, and two smaller pilots). Quick highlights from my side:

- Acme Corp — Pilot complete; commercial pilot extension asked for more latency SLOs. Procurement is looped; they asked for a data processing addendum and a customized SLA. Key ask: executive intro to their CTO. Confidence: Medium (pending SLA redline).
- GammaHealth — Deep evaluation, security review expected to finish next week. Procurement asked for SOC2 evidence (I attached the checklist note). Confidence: Low-to-Med (controls gating).
- Nebula Analytics — Product-led usage is strong; just waiting on purchasing approval from their budget owner (final PO expected within 30 days). Confidence: High.

Question for Connor: for Acme, do we want to carve a short-term pilot pricing discount in the forecast, or show the full list price and apply a potential credit line in handoff? That will shift our consolidated revenue number.

Attachments: acct-onepagers.zip

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Manager, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR play: runway rollup, consolidated forecast, and account walk-throughs

Connor / team —

I pulled a consolidated snapshot and pushed forecast-consolidated.csv to the Drive (sheet: "consolidated_snapshot"). Key numbers (next 90 days):

- Committed ARR rolling in: $3.2M
- Near-term at-risk (Low confidence): $820k
- Net expected: $2.38M (base)

My notes on where the model is sensitive:
- Acme Corp: if we model a 20% pilot discount the expected close slides by ~$220k. Recommend we maintain list price in the public consolidated, and show a separate sensitivity slide with discount scenarios.
- GammaHealth: procurement timeline uncertain; if controls clearance slips >30 days, treat as push to Q1.

Action items for me: I will bake confidence buckets into the consolidated and add a 2-slide sensitivity matrix for discount vs. close probability. Expect update by EOD Tuesday.

Attachments: forecast-consolidated.csv

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR play: runway rollup, consolidated forecast, and account walk-throughs

Connor / Marissa —

Quick note from Acme: procurement is okay to proceed with a short-term pilot discount, but we need the following before legal will sign:

- Draft DPA with data jurisdiction spelled out (we are EU + US users)
- A clear operational runbook and escalation path for incidents during pilot
- A short demo for our CTO (proposed slot: Oct 12–13)

We appreciate the one-pager — can Marissa loop in engineering ops for the runbook, and can Connor confirm who will present for the CTO demo?

Thanks,
Sally Jenkins
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR play: runway rollup, consolidated forecast, and account walk-throughs

Thank you — this is in good shape. A few executive-level asks prior to the deck: 

1) Slide 6 should have the consolidated forecast with confidence tiers visible (High/Med/Low). Rishi, publish a version with the confidence filter applied AND a separate sensitivity slide with the 0/10/20% pilot discount scenarios.
2) Marissa, please ensure the Acme one-pager calls out the runbook owner (ops person) and a tentative CTO demo slot. If procurement needs a DPA template, loop in Legal immediately.
3) Ben, I want a one-paragraph note on capacity/infra readiness if we accelerate Acme to pilot (is there a burst plan?).
4) Connor: I will present the consolidated numbers in the QBR — please be prepared to speak to the top three at-risk deals and mitigation plans.

Deadline: updated Drive materials and final slide deck by EOD Monday so I can rehearse on Tuesday.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Go-to-Market Operations | Redwood Inference
